document.note: Rumsfeld contacts Tenet about the intelligence that led to capturing KSM. He asks whether the information came from GTMO detainees. No response appears in the DOD release.

events.description: Rumsfeld sends Doug Feith a snowflake asking him to review an interview with one of the detainees.
A group appears to have carried out an action in India; the OCR is too garbled to say more.

Rumsfeld sent a memo to Doug Feith, with an undated handwritten detainee interview attached, asking him to look at it and respond. The attachment is a largely illegible handwritten interview about al-Qa'ida, bin Ladin, the Taliban and contingency plans.
A group led by Saeed Sheikh appears to have carried out an action in India in 1994 and made an offer to the Indian authorities. The OCR is too garbled to confirm what happened.
The notes appear to say that bin Ladin returned to Afghanistan, with a stay of about three months mentioned. The OCR is badly garbled, so this is low confidence.

Garbled handwritten notes (OCR) appear to say that in 1994 a group reached India and dealt with an Indian commander, and that its leader was Saeed Sheikh. The reading is low confidence and the details are unclear.

key_claims: The chunk is a Rumsfeld snowflake dated 1 Oct 2002 forwarding a detainee interview to Doug Feith.
The attached handwritten notes are mostly illegible in the OCR; they appear to cover al-Qa'ida leadership, communications and contingency planning, including in Sudan, Afghanistan and Pakistan.
The handwritten notes in this chunk are largely illegible OCR; only fragmentary references to the ISI, the Taliban, al-Qa'ida, Bin Ladin and a 1994 group action are discernible.
This chunk is OCR of handwritten Rumsfeld notes and is almost entirely illegible; no reliable claims about network relationships can be extracted.
The only identifiable name in the chunk is a garbled reference to Usama bin Ladin on p.45.
This chunk consists almost entirely of illegible scans of handwritten notes, so few reliable extractions are possible.
Notes on p.51 apparently refer to Bin Ladin and the Bin Ladin family, with some mention of 1986.
Notes on p.54 apparently mention that 10,000-20,000 people were trained in Afghanistan.
This chunk is almost entirely illegible OCR of handwritten Rumsfeld notes (Bates 11-L-0559/OSD/6888-6889), so no actors, links or events can be reliably extracted.
